PRTree: Exploratory Semi-Synthetic Studies (07 & 08)

Sensitivity Analyses: Standard Missingness vs. Two-Tail Selection in Strong Predictors

PRTree Paper Project

2026-11-08

1 Executive Summary

This report compiles the exploratory semi-synthetic simulation experiments that served as stepping stones prior to the final specification adopted in Section 6 of the paper (Upper-Tail MNAR Missingness):

  1. Study 07 (results_semisynthetic_mech/): Missing values are induced across all predictors under standard MCAR, MAR, and two-tail MNAR mechanisms.
  2. Study 08 (results_semisynthetic_strong/): Missingness is selectively injected into the strongest predictors (highest variance / correlation), removing observations from both tails (lowest and highest values) under MNAR.
  3. Relation to Study 09 (Main Paper): Study 09 refines Study 08 by restricting the MNAR mechanism to the upper tail only (simulating detection/saturation thresholds), which represents the most realistic and asymmetric degradation benchmark.

Both experiments evaluate the three benchmark datasets with complete covariates (Auto MPG, Ozone, and Concrete) across missingness rates \(r \in \{10\%, 25\%, 40\%\}\) over 10 independent replications and 5 folds (50 evaluation runs per condition).

2 1. Study 07: Standard Missingness Across All Predictors

In this study, missing values were induced across all predictors indiscriminately.

2.1 Relative Prediction Error vs. Complete-Data Benchmark

Relative error is defined as: \[\Delta_{\text{full}} = \frac{\text{RMSE} - \text{RMSE}_{\text{PR-full}}}{\text{RMSE}_{\text{PR-full}}}\]

4 3. Comparative Synthesis: 07 vs. 08 vs. 09

Dimension Study 07 (mech) Study 08 (strong) Study 09 (upper - Main Paper)
Affected Predictors All predictors (\(p\)) Strongest \(\lfloor p/2 \rfloor\) predictors Strongest \(\lfloor p/2 \rfloor\) predictors
Fully Observed Predictors None (all subject to missingness) Complementary \(\lceil p/2 \rceil\) predictors Complementary \(\lceil p/2 \rceil\) predictors
MAR Deletion Rule Bilateral: conditioned on extreme absolute values (\(\|Z\|\)) of guide variables Bilateral: conditioned on extreme absolute values (\(\|Z\|\)) of observed predictors Unilateral: conditioned on high positive values (\(Z\)) of observed predictors
MNAR Deletion Rule Two-tail: lowest and highest values removed from each predictor Two-tail: lowest and highest values removed from strong predictors Upper-tail only: highest values removed from strong predictors (simulates sensor saturation)
Role in the Project Initial baseline (exploratory) Sensitivity study (exploratory) Published specification (Section 6 of the paper)

4.1 Summary of PRTree Performance Across Studies

  • Study 07 (Standard Missingness across All Features):
    • PR-f2 systematically outperforms CART-surrogate across all datasets, missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR), and loss rates (\(r \in \{10\%, 25\%, 40\%\}\)).
    • Internal missing-data handling (PR-f2) achieves competitive RMSE with sophisticated multi-stage imputation (MICE+PR, missForest+PR), at a fraction of the computational runtime.
    • Performance degrades smoothly as \(r\) increases from 10% to 40%, demonstrating solid stability when missingness is diffuse.
  • Study 08 (Missingness in Strong Predictors, Two-Tail MNAR):
    • Concentrating missingness in the strongest predictors increases the relative prediction error for all methods compared to Study 07.
    • Despite the loss of key signals at both extremes, PR-f2 preserves predictive accuracy substantially better than CART-surrogate.
    • PR-f2 remains on par with MICE+PR and missForest+PR, confirming that PRTree does not rely on weaker predictors to compensate for missing information in primary features.
  • Study 09 (Main Paper — Upper-Tail MNAR in Strong Predictors):
    • Removing only the upper tail introduces severe asymmetric distribution shifts (censoring at high values), which particularly penalizes mean and kNN imputation.
    • PR-f2 demonstrates clear dominance over CART variants and matches or exceeds computationally heavy imputation pipelines.
    • This progression confirmed the robustness of PRTree under extreme MNAR conditions, which became the cornerstone of Section 6 in the final paper.
